title: Codemode declarations, execution, replay and Remote capability ledger

rows.capability: Codemode source grammar and options prefix
rows.operation: Export the exact `// @options:` prefix and the Lark grammar for the model-facing `code` argument; the grammar only fixes the shape of the optional options line and leaves JSON/code validation to the parser.
rows.consumer: Model-facing `codemode` tool definition, constrained-sampling adapters, and every source parser call.

scenarios: the public options prefix and grammar constants are fixed

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/extensions/codemode/CodemodeSource.hpp:kCodemodeOptionsPrefix,kCodemodeSourceGrammar`; `CodemodeTool.cpp:codemode_tool_definition` attaches the grammar variant.
rows.cppEvidence: `CodemodeParityTest.cpp:107` compares the grammar byte for byte with `fixtures/pi-v1.3.0/codemode-source-grammar.lark`; `CodemodeTool.cpp:69` declares the single `code` string parameter. The capture pins prefix/grammar against v1.3.0.
rows.recommendation: Keep the constants; derive the grammar fixture and the constrained-sampling variant from the same source so a future upstream grammar change cannot update one face only.

rows.capability: Codemode source body and first-line options parsing
rows.operation: Treat the first line as options only when it starts (after leading whitespace) with `// @options:`; replace that line with an empty line so script line numbers do not move; return the untouched input when there is no options line; accept CRLF, an empty object, leading whitespace and a zero token budget.
rows.consumer: The model-facing `codemode` tool execution path, the Application `executeCodemode` wrapper, and any direct parser caller.

scenarios: source keeps plain JavaScript and a leading ordinary comment unchanged
first-line options are parsed and replaced by an empty line to preserve line numbers
options accept leading whitespace, CRLF, an empty object and a zero token budget
only the first line is an options line

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/extensions/codemode/CodemodeSource.cpp:parse_codemode_source` (line 91), `CodemodeSource.hpp:CodemodeSourceOptions`; no dedicated C++ source test.
rows.cppEvidence: The C++ parser implements plain code, first-line options, empty-line replacement, CRLF normalization, zero `max_output_tokens`, and the same SAFE-integer/timeout bounds. Pike has no test for the accepted forms; the capture is upstream-only.
rows.recommendation: Keep the parser. Add the captured accepted-form cases to a focused source test when the parity suite can call the public parser (the module currently has no dedicated test).

rows.capability: Codemode options placement and typed validation errors
rows.operation: Reject an `// @options:` line found after the first line with the exact line number, and reject empty input, invalid JSON, non-object options, unknown fields, invalid `max_output_tokens`/`timeout_ms`, and an options line with no following source as typed `CodemodeSourceError` values.
rows.consumer: The model-facing tool and every caller that turns a validation failure into a `Script error:` result.

scenarios: a misplaced options line is rejected with its line number
invalid options and empty input are rejected with typed errors

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/extensions/codemode/CodemodeSource.cpp:parse_codemode_source` scans only the first line; it returns plain code when a later line starts with the prefix. `parse_source_options` returns `support::ErrorCode::Validation` messages but adds a JSON parse detail that v1.3.0 does not include.
rows.cppEvidence: Pike has no misplaced-line check: `text\n// @options: {}` is accepted as source. The invalid-JSON message is `@options must be valid JSON ...: <parser detail>` where v1.3.0 emits the generic `@options must be a JSON object with supported fields ...`. No C++ test covers either case.
rows.recommendation: Scan for a later first-token `// @options:` line and raise the v1.3.0 line-numbered error; align the invalid-JSON text with the captured generic message. Add both cases to a source test.

rows.capability: Script deadline from the options line
rows.operation: Use `timeout_ms` as the whole-execution deadline; without it the Application passes `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` rather than the library default of 300 s. An expired deadline ends a script that is waiting on a tool as well as one computing, and reports `Execution timed out after <n> ms`.
rows.consumer: Application `executeCodemode`; the model-facing tool result tail; the sandbox timeout path.

sources: packages/codemode/test/sandbox.test.ts:terminates a synchronous infinite loop on timeout
scenarios: a script that computes past its deadline is a timeout
a script failure keeps prior output and reports the script error with its line

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/extensions/codemode/CodemodeSandbox.cpp:875` (`limits.timeout`), `CodemodeToolSource.cpp:limits_for` maps a parsed `timeout_ms` or leaves the timeout disabled; `CodemodeSandbox.cpp:860` formats the timeout.
rows.cppEvidence: `CodemodeSandboxTest.cpp:133` covers a computing runaway with a 150 ms limit. `CodemodeToolSource.cpp:limits_for` correctly makes an absent option infinite like the Application. No test covers a tool-waiting deadline or the exact `Execution timed out after N ms` text.
rows.recommendation: Add a deadline-while-tool-waits case with the exact message to the sandbox/routing tests; keep the default-infinite application rule.

rows.operation: Consume `max_output_tokens` (Application default 10,000 estimated tokens, four characters per token) after joining output text: when over budget, keep head and tail, write the full text to a temp output file, and expose the path as `details.fullOutputPath`.
rows.consumer: Application result formatting and the TUI/fallback renderer.
rows.cppSeam: `CodemodeSource.cpp:76` parses and stores `max_output_tokens`; `CodemodeToolSource.cpp:to_extension_result` never reads it. There is no output joining, truncation, spill file or `fullOutputPath` in the coding-agent path.
rows.cppEvidence: The option is parsed but has no effect. A large script result is returned whole as text; no truncation marker or full-output file is available. This is a structural Application gap, not just a missing test.
rows.recommendation: Implement the Application formatter before adding a differential output-budget test; keep the library parser behavior unchanged.

rows.capability: Identifier normalization for script tool names
rows.operation: Map a registered tool name to its script identifier by replacing invalid identifier characters with `_` and an empty name with `_`, while keeping the raw name available as `tools["<raw>"]`.
rows.consumer: Codemode tool descriptors, `tools.*` bindings, discovery results, catalog headings and declaration rendering.

scenarios: tool identifiers replace invalid characters and preserve MCP names

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/extensions/codemode/CodemodeDiscovery.{hpp,cpp}:to_codemode_identifier`; `CodemodeToolSource.cpp:to_descriptors` derives `js_name` from it and the prelude binds both names.
rows.cppEvidence: `CodemodeRoutingTest.cpp:210` asserts both `tools.list_issues` and `tools["list-issues"]` reach the same session tool. No unit test covers the empty-name or punctuation cases; the C++ implementation has the same replacement rule.
rows.recommendation: Add the captured identifier table to a focused unit test; keep the routing test for the two-name binding.

rows.capability: JSON Schema to TypeScript type rendering
rows.operation: Render JSON Schema primitives, literals, unions, nullable unions, objects, arrays/tuples, local `$ref` resolution, recursive refs as `unknown`, remote refs as `unknown`, property descriptions as comments, and integer/string/`deprecated` tags. Drop tags and then return `unknown` as the character budget is exhausted; keep line terminators escaped.
rows.consumer: Tool declarations, `ALL_TOOLS` samples, discovery `searchTools`/`describeTool` output, and the model-facing catalog.

scenarios: schema primitives, literals, unions and references render as TypeScript types
object properties are sorted on one line with quoted non-identifier keys
property descriptions become comment lines
constraint tags render integer bounds, defaults, patterns and deprecated markers
optional non-null branches keep their constraint tags
draft-04 boolean exclusive bounds become exclusive tags
long tags are dropped, line terminators are escaped, and line breaks stay in comments
types over the character budget drop tags, then become unknown
local references resolve and recursive or remote references render unknown

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/extensions/codemode/CodemodeDiscovery.cpp:schema_to_type` (line 515) over `to_type`, `object_type`, `array_type`, `resolve_ref`; declaration budget at `kDefaultInputSchemaMaxChars`.
rows.cppEvidence: The implementation has the same major rendering branches (references, tuples, comments, tags, budget fallback), but there is no C++ test at all for `schema_to_type`. The captured v1.3.0 fixtures pin the exact rendering, including tag ordering, escaping and the `16,000`-character input-schema budget.
rows.recommendation: Add a typed unit-test table mirroring the captured declarations artifact before treating this as verified; do not fold it into the end-to-end sandbox test.

rows.capability: Tool declaration, signature and output type rendering
rows.operation: Render a tool declaration as `name(args: <input>): Promise<<output>>`, defaulting a missing output schema to `Promise<string>`, and render a standalone output type. `renderToolSample` combines the description and the declaration; `renderToolSignature` omits the description.
rows.consumer: `toCodemodeDeclaration`, `renderDeclarations`, `ALL_TOOLS` descriptions, discovery samples, and codemode catalog sections.

scenarios: tool signatures and samples use the output schema and input budget
renderDeclarations groups tools, globals and namespaces with doc comments

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/extensions/codemode/CodemodeDiscovery.cpp:render_tool_sample` (line 522) hard-codes `Promise<unknown>`; no `render_tool_signature`/`render_tool_output_type`/`render_declarations` exists in `src/coding_agent/extensions/codemode`.
rows.cppEvidence: Pike renders every tool call as `Promise<unknown>`, so a script sees no output type even when the tool declares `outputSchema`. `CodemodeTool.cpp:codemode_description` lists bare property names rather than declarations. There is no public declaration renderer for globals, namespaces, doc comments or output schemas.
rows.recommendation: Add the output-schema-aware declaration/signature renderer and a public `render_declarations` seam before implementing the dynamic catalog. Keep `Promise<string>` as the missing-output default.

rows.operation: Limit the rendered input schema to 16,000 characters (`DEFAULT_INPUT_SCHEMA_MAX_CHARS`): over-budget schemas render as `unknown`, while an explicit alternate budget is honored.
rows.consumer: Tool declarations, discovery samples, catalog sections and script signatures.

scenarios: tool signatures and samples use the output schema and input budget

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodeDiscovery.cpp:kDefaultInputSchemaMaxChars` (16,000) and `schema_to_type(..., max_chars)`; `render_tool_sample` uses it.
rows.cppEvidence: The constant and over-budget fallback exist. There is no C++ test for the 16,000-character boundary or for an alternate budget. The output schema is not rendered at all, so half of the captured declaration budget behavior is absent.
rows.recommendation: Test the input boundary separately from the output-schema work; both belong in the declaration renderer rather than the sandbox.

rows.operation: Build the description from the intro, the globals block, then one section per listed tool with its declaration and guidelines. Group tools by namespace, omit deferred tools entirely, enforce the inline token budget per group with an explicit `(tools not listed)`/`(some tools not listed)` marker, and keep an empty catalog stable.
rows.consumer: The `codemode` model-facing tool description, MCP late-registration refresh, and the loadout/prompt assembly.

scenarios: the empty codemode catalog still declares globals, discovery and the options grammar
a listed tool section carries its declaration, output type and guidelines
namespaces group sections and the inline budget omits tools with an explicit marker
deferred tools are never listed and do not change the description

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/extensions/codemode/CodemodeTool.cpp:codemode_description` (line 43) appends `- tools.<name>({ props })` lines; `McpProductionAdapters.cpp:541` refreshes it with all non-hidden definitions. No namespace, deferred or budget selection exists; prose is the frozen v1.0.4 text.
rows.cppEvidence: The catalog is structurally different from v1.3.0: no fenced declaration, no output type, no guidelines, no namespace heading, no deferred filtering and no inline-budget marker. `SettingsManager::codemode_inline_budget` is parsed but never passed to the description. `CodemodeParityTest.cpp:86` asserts the old bullet form, so the existing test locks in the drift.
rows.recommendation: Replace the bullet renderer with the v1.3.0 catalog and thread mode/inline budget/namespace/deferred metadata into the refresh path. Update the parity test only after the new differential fixture is registered.

rows.capability: Codemode loadout modes and per-tool script descriptions
rows.operation: In `on` mode, give each direct callable tool a `Codemode: tools.<id>(args) resolves to <type>` sentence and list only non-direct callable tools in the codemode catalog. In `only` mode, list every callable tool in the catalog and hide direct declarations. Apply `codemode.mode` from settings.
rows.consumer: Application loadout assembly, system-prompt catalog and direct tool descriptions.

scenarios: the on loadout lists only non-direct callable tools and adds script-call descriptions
the only loadout lists every callable tool and hides direct declarations

rows.cppSeam: No C++ loadout hook: `ExtensionTool` exposes `default_active` and description but no `prepare_loadout`; `SettingsManager.cpp:1398` only stores `codemode_mode`. `AgentMcpToolSurface` updates the single description.
rows.cppEvidence: The mode setting has no consumer. Pike cannot produce per-tool `Codemode:` descriptions, cannot hide direct declarations in `only` mode, and cannot exclude direct tools from the catalog in `on` mode. This is a missing Application seam, not a formatting difference.
rows.recommendation: Add the loadout seam (with exposure/namespace/deferred metadata) before porting the mode tests; keep settings parsing as the input.

rows.operation: When the application enables model access, `models.getAvailableOfType`/`getModelsOfType`/`getModelOfType`/`classify`/`generateImages` select catalog models, account usage, enforce call limits and turn classifier results into prompt text.
rows.consumer: Application codemode tool with a model registry; scripts that classify or generate images.
rows.cppSeam: `CodemodeTool.hpp` states Pike has no `models.*` namespace; there is no provider, classifier or image-generation implementation.
rows.cppEvidence: Excluded from A09: provider execution belongs to the retained AI/model-orchestration contract, not to codemode declaration/execution/replay/Remote. The description-gate capture does not prove provider execution.
rows.recommendation: Do not implement `models.*` provider execution in the codemode port. Track it under the retained AI contract if the product needs it; do not cite the gate capture as proof.

rows.operation: Emit the `models` globals line and classifier/image wording in the `codemode` description only when the tool is created with model access; omit it when models are disabled or absent.
rows.consumer: Model-facing codemode description and system prompt.

scenarios: the models declaration line is present only when models are enabled

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodeTool.cpp:codemode_description` never emits the models line. Pike has no model globals, so the capability-absent branch is the only reachable behavior.
rows.cppEvidence: The absent branch matches the captured gate (`withoutModels: false`), but the enabled branch (`withModels: true`, classifier/image wording) is unsupported. This row covers only that capability-absent behavior; provider execution is the separate excluded row.
rows.recommendation: Keep the absent branch correct and add a differential assertion when the catalog is ported. Do not use this row as a demand to implement model providers.

rows.operation: A script may call every registered tool except `codemode` itself; the description and `ALL_TOOLS` consume the same callable set, filtered for the selected exposure and deferred metadata by the loadout.
rows.consumer: Codemode tool source, discovery globals, catalog description and nested-call routing.

scenarios: the callable tool set excludes codemode itself

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodeToolSource.cpp:callable_tools` filters only `kCodemodeToolName`; `CodemodeDiscovery` is built from that vector.
rows.cppEvidence: The basic exclusion is implemented and exercised indirectly by routing tests. Pike has no explicit callable-set test, and the C++ description refresh additionally filters MCP `Hidden` exposure at the production adapter, not in `callable_tools`.
rows.recommendation: Add a focused test for the exclusion and hidden/deferred interaction; keep the production exposure filter outside the library callable predicate.

rows.operation: Expose every callable tool as an async `tools.<jsName>` and `tools["<raw name>"]` function; route each call through the host nested-call seam, record status/duration, preserve structured results when the tool declares an output schema, and reject missing tools or failures with catchable `Error`s.
rows.consumer: Codemode prelude, `CodemodeSandbox` bridge, `CodemodeToolCallHandler`, the Application nested-call runner and the TUI.

scenarios: tools are async functions under normalized identifiers and record status and duration presence
unknown tools and thrown tool errors are catchable, with error call status

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodeSandbox.cpp:handle_bridge` (`call`/`global`), `CodemodeToolSource.cpp:to_descriptors` + handler, `script_value_from` at line 138, prelude `toolsProxy`; `NestedToolCalls` records the call.
rows.cppEvidence: `CodemodeSandboxTest.cpp:193` covers a routed call; `CodemodeRoutingTest.cpp:181` covers routing/status; `:242`, `:276`, `:304`, `:321` cover structured, error-structured, text-only and fallback failures. The C++ script call record has `arguments` rather than the Application preview string and uses `unfinished` rather than pi `cancelled` for an interrupted call.
rows.recommendation: Keep the routing; align the nested-call record status/arguments with the codemode details shape if the renderer consumes it. Add the captured unknown-tool catch and unawaited-cancel cases.

rows.operation: Bind host globals as top-level identifiers; a `spread` global receives the argument array, and dotted names such as `models.classify` are grouped into a frozen namespace object. Constructor validation rejects invalid identifiers, duplicate names and namespace conflicts.
rows.consumer: Application execute path, discovery globals, model globals, and any host helper attached to a script.

scenarios: globals support top-level spread calls and dotted frozen namespaces
invalid global names, duplicates and namespace conflicts are rejected at construction
globals count as issued calls and rejection properties reach the script Error

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodeSandbox.cpp` passes the literal `no_globals = "[]"` to the prelude (line 786); `CodemodeSandbox::run` has no globals argument. `CodemodeDiscovery::globals_json` exists but is never called.
rows.cppEvidence: The stale prelude can render globals, but the C++ host always gives it an empty list. Scripts cannot see `searchTools`, `describeTool`, `describeNamespace` or any application global; the discovery handler in `CodemodeToolSource.cpp` is therefore unreachable. Constructor-time global validation and numbered global calls are absent.
rows.recommendation: Add a `CodemodeGlobalDescriptor`/globals argument to `CodemodeSandbox::run`, pass `CodemodeDiscovery::globals_json()` plus application globals, and test the captured spread/dotted/validation cases. Do not try to fix discovery without this seam.

rows.operation: Expose BM25-ranked `searchTools(query, {limit, namespace})`, full sample `describeTool(name)` and namespace listing `describeNamespace(name)` over the callable set, returning JSON values to the script.
rows.consumer: Scripts that need unlisted tools (especially MCP tools), the codemode catalog, and the MCP exposure UI copy.

scenarios: the empty codemode catalog still declares globals, discovery and the options grammar
the callable tool set excludes codemode itself

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/extensions/codemode/CodemodeDiscovery.{hpp,cpp}` implements BM25/schema samples and `handle`; `describeNamespace` always returns `null` (line 612); `globals_json` is never wired into the sandbox.
rows.cppEvidence: The library code is substantial but dead: with `globalsJson=[]` no discovery identifier exists in a script. `describeNamespace` is a stub because Pike has no tool namespaces in this seam. There is no C++ test for discovery. The captured v1.3.0 catalog advertises these globals, so the description promises an unavailable API.
rows.recommendation: Wire `globals_json` into the sandbox first, then implement namespace metadata instead of returning `null`; add scripts that call all three globals to routing tests.

rows.operation: Keep a per-run JSON snapshot of stored values; `store(key, value)` validates key/value JSON, per-value and total size limits, and `undefined` deletes; `load(key)` returns parsed JSON or undefined. Only successful executions report `{set,delete}` writes.
rows.consumer: Application session store (`codemode-store` entry), scripts that keep small state across calls, and the result details.

scenarios: store and load use a JSON snapshot and only successful executions report writes
exit() succeeds with prior output and store writes and stops later output

rows.cppSeam: The v1.0.4 prelude in `CodemodePrelude.hpp` implements store/load and size checks, but `CodemodeSandbox.cpp:786` passes `no_store = "{}"` and `emit_done` ignores the writes argument (line 321). `CodemodeRunResult` has no `storeWrites`; `kCodemodeStoreEntryType` is unreferenced outside the constant/test.
rows.cppEvidence: Scripts start from an empty store every run, and even successful writes are discarded. The Application has no branch-read/append path, so the advertised persistence contract is absent end to end. The existing prelude fixture test only proves the prelude text matches the old fixture.
rows.recommendation: Add store input/output to `CodemodeRunResult` and `CodemodeSandbox::run`, then port the Application branch read/append. Test a snapshot, a failed execution that loses writes, and the exit-with-writes case.

rows.operation: Append `text()`/`console.*` as text items and `image()` as image items in production order; mark console items with `console: true`; `text()` JSON-stringifies non-strings and `image()` accepts a data URL, `{image_url}`, or an image block. The extension header/result appends a returned value after prior output.
rows.consumer: Application result formatting, TUI/fallback rendering, image sidecars and output spill.

scenarios: a script returns a JSON value after top-level await and collects output in order
text values are stringified and image accepts data URLs and image blocks
invalid image arguments throw a catchable TypeError inside the script

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodeSandbox.cpp:handle_bridge` maps every non-image channel to `Kind::Text` with no console flag; `CodemodeOutputItem` has only Text/Image. The embedded prelude emits console as `text`; v1.3.0 emits `console`. `CodemodeToolSource.cpp:to_extension_result` appends content in order but has no console block.
rows.cppEvidence: `CodemodeSandboxTest.cpp:92` checks text order/value and `:107` checks image MIME/data. `CodemodeOutputPresentationTest.cpp` checks fallback rendering and image sidecars. Neither can distinguish console output from `text()` because the C++ item has no console field. The v1.3.0 `console: true` channel is lost.
rows.recommendation: Add a console discriminant to `CodemodeOutputItem` and update the prelude to emit `console`; then use it in the Application output block. Keep text/image ordering tests, but assert console separately.

rows.capability: Image helper argument and MIME handling
rows.operation: Accept a non-empty data URL/string, `{image_url}`, or an image block; detect the MIME type from the base64 signature (ignore a misleading data-URI type); reject invalid data with v1.3.0 `TypeError` texts; save displayed images to temp files only in the Application layer.
rows.consumer: Script image output, image fixtures, TUI sidecars and the model result.

scenarios: text values are stringified and image accepts data URLs and image blocks
invalid image arguments throw a catchable TypeError inside the script

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodePrelude.hpp:imageUrl` and `output("image", ...)`; `CodemodeSandbox.cpp:handle_bridge` reads `mimeType` from the bridge. The prelude is v1.0.4 and says `raw MCP image block`, while v1.3.0 says `image block { type: "image", data, mimeType }`.
rows.cppEvidence: `CodemodeSandboxTest.cpp:107` verifies PNG signature detection and base64 stripping. The C++ error strings are the pre-v1.3.0 MCP wording, so a differential script that asserts the captured `TypeError.message` fails. No C++ code saves images to temp files or adds the `[Image saved to ...]` label.
rows.recommendation: Regenerate the prelude from v1.3.0 (or patch the image texts) and add the Application temp-file save/label path. Keep signature detection rather than trusting the data URI.

rows.operation: `exit()` ends the script successfully, keeps output and store writes produced before it, and prevents later output; the result is `value: undefined`.
rows.consumer: Scripts and the Application result formatter.

scenarios: exit() succeeds with prior output and store writes and stops later output

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodePrelude.hpp:exit` calls `done(true, undefined, writesJson)`; `emit_done` keeps prior output but ignores the writes argument (`CodemodeSandbox.cpp:321`).
rows.cppEvidence: The control-flow exit and prior output work. Store writes from the exit payload are dropped, so the captured `exit()` contract is only partially implemented. No C++ test exercises `exit()`.
rows.recommendation: Carry the writes through `emit_done` as part of the store work; add an exit-with-output-and-writes test.

rows.capability: Script error names, stacks, kinds and catchability
rows.operation: Report a script `Error` with `kind: "script"`, name, message and stack in `codemode.js:line:col` form; syntax errors, non-Error throws, BigInt serialization, unknown tools, out-of-memory and tool failures must be catchable inside the script where applicable, while a terminal syntax error settles the run.
rows.consumer: Application error formatting, model-facing `Script error:` block and the TUI.

scenarios: a script failure keeps prior output and reports the script error with its line
non-Error throws, syntax errors and non-serializable returns are script errors
a memory-limited VM reports out of memory as a script error
unknown tools and thrown tool errors are catchable, with error call status

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodeError` in `CodemodeSandbox.hpp` stores only `kind` and `message`; `CodemodeSandbox.cpp:emit_done`/`message_from` parse a message object but do not retain `name`/`stack`; `g.exception_text()` supplies a text stack for syntax errors.
rows.cppEvidence: Pike preserves the script error text, including a stack, in `message`, but has no typed `name`/`stack` fields. `CodemodeSandboxTest.cpp:122` only checks the message substring for a thrown Error. Captured BigInt, non-Error, syntax, unknown-tool and OOM shapes cannot be represented exactly in the C++ result type.
rows.recommendation: Extend `CodemodeError` with optional name/stack and parse the prelude payload; test the captured taxonomy through the public result rather than only `message.find`.

rows.operation: Public constants `MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=16,777,216`, `MAX_OUTPUT_ITEMS=100,000`, `MAX_STORE_VALUE_CHARS=262,144`, and `MAX_STORE_TOTAL_CHARS=1,048,576`; exceeding an output limit fails the script with a `RangeError`, and store limits are enforced per value and total.
rows.consumer: Script output collection, store snapshots and the stable prelude fingerprint.

scenarios: the guest prelude is the frozen sandbox prelude with output and store limits

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodePrelude.hpp:302-318` enforces the same numeric output limits; store checks at the prelude store function. C++ exposes the constants only inside the prelude, not as public C++ constants.
rows.cppEvidence: The embedded v1.0.4 prelude has the same output/store numeric limits as v1.3.0. `CodemodePrelude.hpp` is a generated literal; the sandbox test only compares it to the old committed fixture, not to the v1.3.0 prelude. There are no C++ limit tests.
rows.recommendation: Pin the prelude to v1.3.0 and add limit tests that cross the boundary; do not expose duplicated C++ constants unless a caller needs them.

rows.capability: Unawaited tool calls at script completion
rows.operation: When the script returns/throws/exits while a tool call is still pending, abort that call and report it as `cancelled`; do not let it keep running after the script result.
rows.consumer: Scripts that fire-and-forget, the Application nested-call record and the TUI status row.

sources: packages/codemode/test/sandbox.test.ts:aborts unawaited calls when the script returns
scenarios: an unawaited tool call is aborted when the script returns and its record is cancelled

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodePrelude.hpp` wraps tool promises and tracks pending calls; `CodemodeSandbox.cpp` stops dispatching when the run is finished; `NestedToolCalls` marks an unfinished call `unfinished`, not `cancelled`.
rows.cppEvidence: The sandbox's prelude can abort and `CodemodeSandboxTest.cpp` has a related script case, but the C++ public result has no call records; the Application nested-call status for an interrupted call is `unfinished`. The captured `status: "cancelled"` and duration presence are not represented in the C++ result type.
rows.recommendation: Map an unfinished nested call to `cancelled` at the codemode result boundary and test the Application details; keep the prelude abort behavior.

rows.capability: Host clock and timezone in non-deterministic execution
rows.operation: A normal `execute()` reads the real wall clock and host timezone; only `start()`/deterministic mode freezes the clock to UTC and the virtual `startedAt`.
rows.consumer: Scripts that use `Date.now()`, `new Date()` or `performance.now()`, and deterministic replay.

scenarios: execute() is not deterministic while start() is
deterministic runs use a virtual UTC clock and seeded randomness without WeakRef

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodeSandbox.cpp:host_get_timezone_offset` always returns 0; the prelude uses QuickJS `Date` for wall time. There is no virtual clock/seed mode.
rows.cppEvidence: A normal run in Pike is always UTC, regardless of the host timezone, and there is no distinction between normal and deterministic time. `Date.now()` is real, but the timezone is pinned. No C++ test covers timezone behavior.

rows.consumer: Session tool assembly, activation/selection and system prompt.

scenarios: the extension registers an inactive model-only codemode tool with the source grammar
the callable tool set excludes codemode itself

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodeToolSource.cpp:167` builds `CodemodeTool` with `default_active=false`, prompt snippet/guidelines, exclusive concurrency and lazy `GuestHolder`; `SessionFactory.cpp:1752` adds the source.
rows.cppEvidence: `CodemodeParityTest.cpp:120` compares name/label/exposure/store type/inline budget/options prefix/description/parameters/grammar/snippet against the pi-v1.0.4 bundle; `:153` checks one contributed tool. The registration shape is implemented; the comparison bundle is stale v1.0.4 and `CodemodeOutputPresentationTest.cpp` shows the lazy load only indirectly.
rows.recommendation: Keep registration; refresh the parity bundle to v1.3.0 before using it as proof of description/snippet parity. Add a direct assertion that load_tools never opens the guest.

rows.operation: Resolve merged `codemode.mode` (`on` default) and `codemode.inlineBudget` with per-field project/global merge, and feed both to the loadout/catalog.
rows.consumer: Application settings and codemode loadout.

scenarios: the on loadout lists only non-direct callable tools and adds script-call descriptions
namespaces group sections and the inline budget omits tools with an explicit marker

rows.cppSeam: `SettingsManager.cpp:1398-1408` resolves both values; `:868-877` merges the nested object. No consumer passes them to codemode.
rows.cppEvidence: `SettingsManagerTest.cpp:888` verifies default/global/project/unknown values. The values are parsed correctly but unused, so settings tests give a false sense of integration coverage.
rows.recommendation: Feed both settings into the loadout/catalog and add an integration assertion that a project `codemode.mode=only` changes the description.

rows.capability: Late tool registration and description refresh
rows.operation: When an MCP server registers tools after session assembly, refresh the codemode description from the live callable set; tools hidden by exposure must not appear, and the codemode tool itself must not be nested.
rows.consumer: Application MCP surface, codemode catalog and MCP exposure management.

scenarios: the empty codemode catalog still declares globals, discovery and the options grammar
namespaces group sections and the inline budget omits tools with an explicit marker

rows.cppSeam: `McpProductionAdapters.cpp:541-550` rebuilds the old bullet description from every non-hidden definition and updates the agent tool description.
rows.cppEvidence: The refresh hook exists but the description renderer is stale and has no namespace/budget/deferred metadata. It calls `codemode_description` with all definitions, so a large MCP catalog is not budget-limited. No test covers a late registration changing the codemode description.
rows.recommendation: Keep the live refresh trigger; swap in the v1.3.0 catalog and thread namespace/exposure metadata from `AgentMcpToolSurface`. Test a late tool registration and a hidden tool.

rows.operation: Format the tool result as `Script completed|failed`, wall time, `Output:`, the formatted output (adjacent text joined, console block, images with temp-path labels), a returned value, the error stack plus call summary on failure, and `details.calls`/`fullOutputPath` for the renderer.
rows.consumer: Model-facing result, TUI renderer, session transcript and output spill.

scenarios: a script returns a JSON value after top-level await and collects output in order
exit() succeeds with prior output and store writes and stops later output
a script failure keeps prior output and reports the script error with its line

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodeToolSource.cpp:to_extension_result` emits header, content items, value/error text; no details, call summary, output joining/truncation, image temp files or console block. `CodemodeOutputPresentationTest.cpp` verifies only the fallback renderer and image sidecar.
rows.cppEvidence: The C++ presentation is the old fallback shape: no nested-call rows, no elapsed timer, no `fullOutputPath`, no `[Image saved to ...]` labels. `ToolResultMessage.nested_calls` exists but the codemode result does not put calls in `details`, and the renderer has no codemode-specific rows. This is a consumer gap even when the sandbox output is correct.
rows.recommendation: Port the Application formatter and renderer details together; keep the fallback for unregistered names but add the codemode details shape. Test the captured header/error/call-summary and image label.

rows.operation: Read the branch’s `codemode-store` entries into the next script’s store snapshot; after a successful script, append one entry with `{set,delete}` only when there are writes. The entry is durable/session state, not part of the library sandbox.
rows.consumer: Application session manager, branch replay/fork and scripts using `store()`/`load()`.

scenarios: store and load use a JSON snapshot and only successful executions report writes
exit() succeeds with prior output and store writes and stops later output

rows.cppSeam: `kCodemodeStoreEntryType` exists only as a constant in `CodemodeTool.hpp:24`; no read/append path and no store snapshot in `CodemodeSandbox`.
rows.cppEvidence: The session entry is entirely missing. Even if the prelude store were wired, a later codemode call would start empty and writes would be dropped. Branch/fork merge behavior is also absent.
rows.recommendation: Implement after the library store snapshot/write result; test cross-call persistence, a failed execution that appends nothing, and branch replay.

rows.capability: Application nested call details and cancellation
rows.operation: Record each script tool call as a `CodemodeNestedCall` with id/name/args preview/status/duration/error; publish updates while the script runs; mark still-running calls `cancelled` when the script ends; show them in the TUI and include a call summary in the failure text.
rows.consumer: Application execute wrapper, TUI renderer and session transcript.

scenarios: an unawaited tool call is aborted when the script returns and its record is cancelled
unknown tools and thrown tool errors are catchable, with error call status

rows.cppSeam: `Agent::NestedToolCalls` records id/name/status/duration/arguments for every nested call and `nested_calls_to_json` serializes it; `CodemodeToolSource.cpp` does not map it into `CodemodeToolDetails`; no renderer uses it.
rows.cppEvidence: `CodemodeRoutingTest.cpp:181` checks the record after a full run, but the shape is `arguments`/`unfinished` rather than the Application preview/`cancelled`, and no UI or failure summary consumes it. Live `publish()`-style progress is absent.
rows.recommendation: Map the generic nested-call record into codemode details and use it in the renderer/failure summary; align status terms and truncate the args preview. Keep the generic record as the source of truth.

rows.capability: Application image saving and model presentation
rows.operation: After a successful script, add a `[Image saved to <path> (<type>, <size>)]` text item before each image, de-duplicate repeated images, and surface images as inline sidecars; a save failure becomes a label rather than losing the result.
rows.consumer: Model result, TUI sidecars, output files and image-heavy scripts.

scenarios: text values are stringified and image accepts data URLs and image blocks

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodeToolSource.cpp:to_extension_result` emits `ai::image_content` directly; no output file or label. `CodemodeOutputPresentationTest.cpp` checks the image sidecar bytes and MIME but not a saved path.
rows.cppEvidence: The model receives image blocks but no file path and no save-failure handling. This matches the old fallback behavior, not the v1.3.0 Application contract.
rows.recommendation: Add the Application save/label step after the output formatter; keep the sandbox’s image bytes unchanged. Test a duplicate image and a write failure.

rows.operation: Append each callable tool’s trimmed prompt guidelines as `- ...` bullets to its declaration description; empty/whitespace guidelines are ignored; the system prompt only contains guidelines for declared tools.
rows.consumer: Codemode catalog, `ALL_TOOLS` samples, discovery descriptions and direct-tool script descriptions.

scenarios: a tool declaration defaults its output schema to string and appends prompt guidelines
a listed tool section carries its declaration, output type and guidelines

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodeToolSource.cpp:to_descriptors` passes `render_tool_sample(tool)` with no guidelines; `CodemodeDiscovery` has no guidelines map. `CodemodeTool.cpp:codemode_description` uses `tool.description` only.
rows.cppEvidence: Guidelines are absent from every codemode description/sample. The C++ Tool definition may carry guidelines elsewhere, but the codemode declaration does not append them, so the captured `- Search before reading.` section cannot appear.
rows.recommendation: Thread the guideline map into the declaration renderer used by the tool source/discovery/catalog; test trimmed bullet insertion and an empty guideline.

rows.capability: Deferred tools in the codemode catalog
rows.operation: Tools with `deferred` exposure remain callable but are never listed; changing only deferred tools must leave the description byte-identical so late registration stays stable.
rows.consumer: Codemode catalog/loadout and MCP late-registration behavior.

scenarios: deferred tools are never listed and do not change the description

rows.cppSeam: No deferred concept in `CodemodeToolSource.cpp`/`CodemodeDiscovery`; the description refresh includes every non-hidden definition.
rows.cppEvidence: Pike cannot defer a callable tool. The captured stability guarantee (the description does not change when only deferred tools are registered) is absent, so a late MCP registration will always grow the catalog.
rows.recommendation: Add deferred metadata to the codemode loadout and filter it before rendering; test the byte-identical description with and without a deferred tool.

rows.operation: Pass `SettingsManager.codemode.inlineBudget` to the catalog; when unset use `DEFAULT_CODEMODE_INLINE_BUDGET=3000`, not a hard-coded unlimited list.
rows.consumer: Codemode catalog, system prompt size and MCP late registration.

scenarios: namespaces group sections and the inline budget omits tools with an explicit marker

rows.cppSeam: `SettingsManager.cpp:1404` and `CodemodeTool.hpp:kCodemodeDefaultInlineBudget` exist; `CodemodeTool.cpp:codemode_description` has no budget parameter.
rows.cppEvidence: Both the setting and the default constant are dead in the renderer. The C++ catalog is unbounded, so a large MCP/tool set can produce a huge description. `CodemodeParityTest.cpp:131` only checks the constant.
rows.recommendation: Consume the setting in the catalog renderer and test the default and a tiny budget; do not leave the constant as the only artifact.

rows.capability: Tool namespaces in the catalog and discovery
rows.operation: Group catalog sections by namespace (tools without a namespace first, then namespaces by name), include the namespace description, expose namespace listings through `describeNamespace`, and keep `searchTools` namespace filtering.
rows.consumer: Codemode catalog, MCP server grouping and scripts discovering MCP tools.

scenarios: namespaces group sections and the inline budget omits tools with an explicit marker

rows.cppSeam: `McpProductionAdapters` stores a `namespace_name`, but `CodemodeTool.cpp` and `CodemodeDiscovery::describeNamespace` do not consume it; `describeNamespace` always returns null.
rows.cppEvidence: Pike has the raw MCP server name in the production adapter but no library namespace type or catalog grouping. The captured `## docs` heading and namespace discovery are absent.
rows.recommendation: Thread namespace metadata from the MCP surface into the library catalog/discovery; implement `describeNamespace` rather than returning null. Test a namespaced and an unnamespaced tool together.

rows.operation: The loadout distinguishes `direct` tools (model sees the tool, script can still call it) from `codemode`/non-direct tools (listed in the codemode catalog); hidden tools are neither. The choice changes the catalog and per-tool descriptions, not script callability.
rows.consumer: MCP exposure management, system prompt budget and scripts.

scenarios: the on loadout lists only non-direct callable tools and adds script-call descriptions
the only loadout lists every callable tool and hides direct declarations
the callable tool set excludes codemode itself

rows.cppSeam: `McpProductionAdapters.cpp:541` filters only `Hidden`; `CodemodeToolSource.cpp` gets all registry tools. No direct/on/only distinction exists in the description path.
rows.cppEvidence: Pike exposes direct tools to the model and lists the same tools in the codemode catalog; there is no `on`/`only` split. The setting row and the loadout row describe the same missing consumer from different angles.
rows.recommendation: Implement exposure metadata in the loadout/catalog before changing MCP exposure behavior; keep hidden tools out of both paths.

rows.capability: Application failure text and call summary
rows.operation: On failure, format the stack for script errors, prefix timeout/abort/sandbox messages, then append `Tool calls made before the failure (they are not undone): name (status), ...` or `No tool calls were made.`
rows.consumer: Model-facing tool result and TUI error rows.

rows.cppSeam: `CodemodeToolSource.cpp:to_extension_result` emits `Script error:\n` plus the sandbox message only; no call summary or kind-specific prefix.
rows.cppEvidence: The failure text is substantially shorter than v1.3.0: no timeout/abort/sandbox prefixes and no record of calls that already ran. A model cannot see which tool effects happened before a failure.
rows.recommendation: Port `formatError`/`formatCallSummary` with the Application nested-call records; test script, timeout, abort, sandbox and no-call variants.
